prerequisites: Python functions, exceptions and context managers
URLs, headers, query strings and JSON
objectives: Choose Requests for synchronous HTTP/1.1 client workflows and recognize when async or HTTP/2 alternatives are more appropriate.
Build robust GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD and OPTIONS requests.
Handle query parameters, form bodies, JSON bodies, multipart uploads, response encodings and binary content.
Use Session objects for connection reuse, cookie persistence, shared headers and authentication.
Apply explicit connect/read timeouts, status validation, bounded retries and safe error handling.
Configure TLS verification, client certificates, proxies and custom transport adapters without weakening security.
Stream large responses safely and close response resources deterministically.
Test HTTP client behavior with deterministic mocks, local test servers and contract fixtures.
Profile latency, connection reuse, memory use and retry behavior under representative workloads.
Explain version-specific API changes and preserve reproducible dependency constraints.

concepts.name: Request/Response model
concepts.explanation: A request describes an HTTP method, URL, headers, query parameters and optional body. Requests sends it and returns a Response with status, headers, body accessors, URL and redirect history.
concepts.analogy: A typed message sent to a remote service and a structured receipt returned.
limitations: A successful transport does not imply the application-level operation succeeded.

concepts.name: Session and connection pooling
concepts.explanation: A Session persists cookies and configuration and reuses underlying connections through urllib3 when the server and response lifecycle permit it.
concepts.analogy: A reusable service desk rather than opening a new counter for every interaction.
limitations: Sessions should not be shared across concurrent workers without a deliberate thread-safety strategy.
Unconsumed streamed responses can tie up pooled connections.

concepts.name: Timeout semantics
concepts.explanation: Requests supports connect/read timeout configuration. The read timeout is an inactivity interval between received bytes, not a hard total wall-clock deadline for the complete download.
concepts.analogy: A maximum wait for the connection and a maximum silence interval while receiving.
limitations: No timeout is applied by default.
A caller needing a total deadline must enforce one at a higher orchestration layer.

concepts.name: Status and exception handling
concepts.explanation: Network failures raise RequestException subclasses. HTTP status failures are not automatically raised by every call; raise_for_status provides explicit status validation.
concepts.analogy: Separate whether the message arrived from whether the service accepted the operation.
limitations: JSON decoding can fail even on a successful HTTP status.
Retrying non-idempotent operations can duplicate side effects.

concepts.name: Streaming and resource lifecycle
concepts.explanation: stream=True allows incremental response consumption; callers must consume or close responses so connections can return to the pool.
concepts.analogy: Read a large file in chunks instead of loading the whole file into memory.
limitations: Streaming does not itself provide integrity verification or safe file destination handling.
Always impose size and time budgets.

concepts.name: Transport adapters
concepts.explanation: HTTPAdapter and mounted adapters customize connection pools and transport behavior for URL prefixes, including retry policy when configured with urllib3 utilities.
concepts.analogy: A replaceable network engine behind a stable request interface.
limitations: Retry semantics must match HTTP method idempotency and application behavior.
Adapter internals and urllib3 compatibility are version-sensitive.

concepts.name: TLS verification and certificates
concepts.explanation: Requests verifies server certificates by default and supports CA bundle paths and client-side certificates for mutual TLS.
concepts.analogy: Verify the server's identity and optionally present the client's identity.
limitations: Disabling verification exposes the connection to interception.
Certificate and proxy configuration are environment-sensitive.

use_cases.scenario: Call JSON REST APIs from scripts and services.
use_cases.implementation_pattern: Use requests.get/post with params or json, explicit timeout, status validation and response.json handling.
tradeoffs: Requires careful retry and deadline policy

use_cases.scenario: Build a shared authenticated API client.
use_cases.implementation_pattern: Wrap a configured Session with base headers, authentication, bounded timeouts, structured logging and explicit close lifecycle.
tradeoffs: Credential refresh belongs in an explicit auth layer

use_cases.implementation_pattern: Use multipart file uploads or stream=True with chunked reads, byte limits, checksums and atomic file replacement.
tradeoffs: Retries need resumability or idempotent semantics

use_cases.scenario: Apply custom transport policy for a specific API host.
use_cases.implementation_pattern: Mount a custom HTTPAdapter on a host prefix with connection pool sizing and a bounded, method-aware retry strategy.

use_cases.scenario: Integrate with Hugging Face Hub or other model/dataset metadata APIs.
use_cases.implementation_pattern: Use Requests only as a synchronous transport layer; keep authentication, pagination, response validation, dataset/model rights review and provenance in separate components.
tradeoffs: Does not replace official client libraries when they provide richer semantics
A metadata API response never grants download or training permission

use_cases.scenario: Generate an adaptive API client from a reviewed OpenAPI description and use Requests for transport.
use_cases.implementation_pattern: Compile a typed client from a pinned OpenAPI schema, validate inputs locally, call through a single policy-controlled Session, and compare generated calls against contract tests.
tradeoffs: Schema drift can break generated clients
Must prevent untrusted schema from creating arbitrary network destinations

architecture_patterns.pattern: One Session per worker or service client
architecture_patterns.when_to_use: Repeated calls to the same hosts with shared auth, headers or cookies.
Read-heavy API clients with documented retryable status codes and idempotent methods.
Large downloads where memory must remain bounded.

threats: Credentials leaked in URLs or logs
safe_defaults: Validate destination hosts against allowlists when URLs are user-controlled
Redact Authorization, Cookie and proxy credentials
Bound response sizes and download time
security.secret_handling: Use a dedicated secret store or environment injection; never hardcode tokens, log authorization headers, or place secrets in query strings.
supply_chain: Pin dependency versions and hashes in production lockfiles
Review Requests and urllib3 release notes
Use trusted package indexes and verify provenance where available

profiling_methods: Measure connect time, time to first byte, total duration and payload size separately
Compare Session reuse with one-shot calls
Measure peak memory for streamed versus buffered downloads
Record retry counts and connection-pool saturation
scaling_limits: Synchronous calls block their calling thread
Use bounded worker pools for concurrency
For async workloads evaluate HTTPX or aiohttp rather than wrapping unlimited threads
performance.cost_model: Requests is an open-source client library; operational cost comes from network calls, server usage, retries, compute, bandwidth and storage.

steps: Create a GET request with query parameters.
Parse JSON and handle decoding errors separately.
verification: A deterministic test verifies query encoding, status handling and timeout propagation.

steps: Add a wrapper that applies bounded timeouts.
Close the session when the client lifecycle ends.
verification: Tests prove headers persist, cookies are retained and secrets are redacted.

exercises.prompt: Write a function that fetches JSON from a supplied HTTPS URL using query parameters, a timeout and status validation.
Build a Session-backed API client with token injection, pagination and safe structured logging.
acceptance_criteria: Request count and errors are observable

exercises.prompt: Implement a bounded streaming download service with SHA-256 verification, size limits and atomic output replacement.

projects.name: DreamCo API Connector
projects.deliverable: A reusable, typed, Session-backed HTTP client with configurable auth, pagination, timeouts, structured telemetry and contract tests.

projects.name: Safe Metadata Harvester
projects.deliverable: A bounded metadata-only harvester that consumes allowlisted public APIs and records provenance without downloading package source or executing code.

diagnosis: Measure time to first byte and inter-byte gaps
Check payload size and server latency
fix: Tune read timeout within a total request deadline
prevention: Enforce request budgets and alert on tail latency

diagnosis: Inspect status code and redacted response metadata
fix: Retry only when policy and idempotency allow
prevention: Status-specific error handling and circuit breaking

diagnosis: Verify trusted CA bundle and proxy settings
fix: Repair trust configuration; never disable verification as a workaround
prevention: Certificate monitoring and secure proxy configuration

diagnosis: Measure active workers and pool waits
fix: Use context managers or close responses
Bound concurrency and configure adapter pools
prevention: Resource lifecycle tests and pool telemetry

innovation.hypothesis: A schema-generated typed client with policy-controlled Requests transport can reduce integration defects compared with handwritten request wrappers.
innovation.baseline: Handwritten Session wrapper with the same endpoints and tests.
innovation.experiment: Generate a client from a pinned OpenAPI schema; add host allowlists, validation, retries and contract tests; compare defect rate and latency on held-out API fixtures.
innovation.risk_review: Untrusted schemas must not control arbitrary destinations or inject executable code; all calls remain sandboxed and metadata-only during evaluation.
innovation.evaluation: Compare correctness, invalid-request rejection, latency, maintainability and security test results; retain as hypothesis until reproduced.

evaluation.target_benchmark: DreamCo HTTP client reliability benchmark: status handling, timeout behavior, auth redaction, pagination, retries, streaming and connection lifecycle.
evaluation.holdout: Unseen HTTP fixtures and failure injection scenarios, not used while authoring exercises.
evaluation.regression: Requests 2.34.2 API compatibility, security controls, response cleanup and existing DreamCo connector tests.
